solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Keep asking family for carriage after midnight

blocks.note: to pump someone is to keep questioning them for information
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Someone persistently begs relatives to drive them home late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Cinderella story the fairy godmother's coach turns back into a pumpkin when the clock strikes twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella's coach reverts to a gourd at midnight, so a playful periphrasis for that vegetable is the carriage after twelve.

clue.text: Ignoring service, doesn't respect note from employer

indicators.note: ignoring a word means leaving it out of the phrase the rest of the clue describes

blocks.note: someone who pays lip service gives only token respect
this word is the one dropped from the end of the phrase

explanation.surface: A worker who skips church shows contempt for a memo from the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: To pay lip service is to express support without meaning it; dropping the last word leaves a phrase that reads as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A payslip is the statement an employer issues with wages, so it is a note from one's employer.

clue.text: Extremely busy girl struggling with a piece of music

indicators.note: something struggling is thrown into disorder, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: a mad day is a hectically busy one
taken as written, part of the rearranged letters
taken as written, part of the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A harried young woman wrestles with a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling with' seems to pair the girl with the music, but 'with a' just adds a letter to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a short part-song for several voices, popular in the Renaissance, so a piece of music.

clue.text: Well, peer almost fixed up credit

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off
in a down entry, putting something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: 'so' and 'well' are both sentence openers
a duke is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman's nearly arranged financial loan, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise or prestige for an achievement, which is credit in the sense of recognition.

clue.text: Nest turned up full of rats? None of your business

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
a thing full of something holds it inside

blocks.note: a den is an animal's lair or nest
rats are an example of vermin, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a rat-infested nest and is told to keep their nose out.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Never mind' can brush off a question, telling the asker it is not their concern.

clue.text: Very keen intent to dump one pompous girl

indicators.note: dumping one means discarding the letter standing for the number one

blocks.note: mad about something is very keen on it
an aim is an intent or purpose
the Roman numeral for one, which is removed

explanation.surface: An overeager person plans to drop a friend who is a stuck-up young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam is an informal term for a conceited or bossy young girl, as in 'little madam'.

clue.text: A soldier, one taking part in WW1 battle

indicators.note: something taking part in an event is inside it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the Battles of the Marne were fought in France in 1914 and 1918

explanation.surface: A soldier is described as one of those who fought in a First World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier serving with a navy, so 'a soldier' covers it.

clue.text: Godlike experience at last provided in bedroom

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding word
in means the preceding letters are placed inside what follows

blocks.note: the last letter of this word
'if' and 'provided' both state a condition
a dorm is a dormitory, a shared bedroom

explanation.surface: Someone finally has a divine experience, so long as it happens in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Deiform means having the form of a god, which is to say godlike.

clue.text: Old American never embraced by woman, it's implied?

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside the arms of another

blocks.note: ay or aye is an old word for ever; the clue's 'never' is its opposite
the clue's 'woman' is the partner of the word actually needed
surface padding that admits the clue states the reverse of what is meant

explanation.surface: Someone who has never been hugged by a woman is hinted at, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay works in reverse: 'ever embraced by man' would build the answer, so the setter says the opposite, never by a woman, and 'it's implied' admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya were the pre-Columbian civilisation of Central America, so a Mayan is an ancient American.

clue.text: Gay Swede worried, so unable to get a word in?

definitions.text: unable to get a word in?

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian is anxious because a talkative companion leaves no room in the conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the familiar idiom with its last word missing; the question mark flags that it is completed by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot get a word in edgeways is shut out of a conversation, so the answer completes the phrase.

clue.text: Selling no alcohol? Notice wood spirit

blocks.note: a dry bar or town sells no alcohol
an ad is a public notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A sign at a teetotal venue apparently advertises a spirit made from wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drink called wood spirit, which a dry place would not sell; here the spirit is a mythical being.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology a dryad is a nymph who lives in trees, a woodland spirit.

clue.text: To spread my wings, I had turned to write poetry

indicators.note: something turned around runs the other way, so these letters are read backwards

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
to versify is to write verse

explanation.surface: Someone describes branching out by taking up writing poems.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread one's wings is to branch out into new ventures, which is what diversifying means; the infinitive matches.

clue.text: Even in pencil, makes public sweet little items

indicators.note: even means the second, fourth and sixth positions of the following word are kept

blocks.note: the even-numbered letters of this word
to air views is to make them public

explanation.surface: Someone sketching in pencil reveals some fine details.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are small cream-filled pastries, so they are sweet little items in a cake shop.

clue.text: Seek and find in dilapidated condition

blocks.note: first meaning: to track someone down after a search
second meaning: neglected and decaying

explanation.surface: A search ends with the discovery of something in a shabby state.
explanation.definitionFit: To run down a fugitive is to hunt and catch them, and a run-down building is shabby and neglected.

clue.text: Sort of order British installed in restored caliphate

indicators.note: something installed is put inside something else
restored suggests the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of this word, rearranged
B is the standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A British figure is put in charge of a reconstituted Islamic state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabetic order is one way of sorting things, by the sequence of letters A to Z.

clue.text: Man of the world, wretch regularly visiting area of London

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one
a visitor goes inside someone else's place

blocks.note: Ealing is a borough of west London
the second, fourth and sixth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A sophisticate and a poor wretch both often call on a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the world' looks like a worldly sophisticate; read literally, it is any human from planet Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthling is an inhabitant of the Earth, so literally a man of the world.

clue.text: Sign of submariner's return

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: Something signals that a submarine crewman is coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent of what is to come.

clue.text: Philistine stripped and thrashed sceptic

indicators.note: something stripped has its outer layer removed, so the first and last letters go
thrashed means beaten about, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: this word without its outside letters

explanation.surface: An uncultured person was undressed and beaten by a doubter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist rejects all moral and religious principles, an extreme kind of sceptic.

clue.text: Communication about university building and grounds in legal terms

definitions.text: building and grounds in legal terms

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a message is a communication
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A memo concerns the legal status of a campus's buildings and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Messuage is a conveyancing term for a dwelling house with its outbuildings and land.

clue.text: A bit of a problem in one's ear

indicators.note: something in one's ear is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone has a minor ear complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Some is a determiner meaning a certain amount of, so 'some bread' is a bit of bread.

clue.text: Early spring: keep in seaside resort

blocks.note: Mar is short for March, the first month of spring
to gate a pupil at boarding school is to confine them to the premises as punishment

explanation.surface: The advice is to stay put at the coast while spring is still young.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGATE is a seaside town in Kent; 'gate' meaning confine is British school slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a traditional English holiday town on the Kent coast, so it is a seaside resort.

clue.text: Ride — up the aisle, do we hear?

indicators.note: asking whether we hear it signals that the words are judged by sound

blocks.note: the route a bride takes up the aisle is a bridal path

explanation.surface: A wedding guest wonders whether the bride will come up the aisle on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: A ride is a track for horse-riding, especially through woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a path made for riding horses, which is exactly what a bridle path is.

clue.text: Emergency transport's appearance, a free ride

blocks.note: an air is a manner or appearance, as in an air of calm
a lift is a free ride in someone's car

explanation.surface: An ambulance shows up and offers a ride without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift moves people or supplies by aircraft, typically in an emergency.

clue.text: Where exhibits are of medium benefit? Not sure

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothes labels
use is benefit, as in 'what's the use?'
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A courtroom doubts whether the evidence is of any real help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhibits' suggests items of evidence in court; here they are things on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum is a building where artefacts are put on display, so it is where exhibits are.

clue.text: Boat half removed by hooligan — it may have been chartered

indicators.note: removing half of a word cuts off half its letters, here the back half

blocks.note: the first half of this word
a rough is a violent hooligan

explanation.surface: A boat damaged by a vandal turns out to have been a hired vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chartered' suggests hiring a boat; here it means granted a royal charter, as a chartered borough was.
explanation.definitionFit: Many English towns became boroughs by royal charter, so a borough is a thing that may have been chartered.

clue.text: Ground's breadth unchanged

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for breadth
'as is' means in the present state, unchanged

explanation.surface: The width of a plot of land remains the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the grounds for something, as in 'on what basis?', so ground in the foundation sense.

clue.text: Quite a blow as aborted process throws one out

indicators.note: throwing out one means discarding the letter standing for the number one

blocks.note: a mistrial is a trial abandoned because of an error

explanation.surface: A collapsed court case is a real setback when a defendant is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a setback; it is a wind. The mistral is a strong cold north wind in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong, violent wind, so it is quite a blow in the gale sense.

clue.text: Hoarder's never-ending distress

indicators.note: something never-ending lacks its end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: misery is deep distress

explanation.surface: Someone who stockpiles things suffers constant anguish.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and possessions, refusing to spend, so a hoarder.

clue.text: Josh succeeded joining available Chinese course

blocks.note: something spare is available for use
to josh or rib someone is to tease them
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A man named Josh managed to get a place on a Chinese studies course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Josh' reads as a man's name, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare ribs are a common dish on Chinese restaurant menus, so they serve as a course of a Chinese meal.

clue.text: Sign is inconsistent? Not very

indicators.note: 'not very' asks for the abbreviation for very to be taken away

blocks.note: something that varies is inconsistent
V is the abbreviation for very, which is removed

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a signal is unreliable, though only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Check covers a source of power

indicators.note: a thing that covers another wraps around it

blocks.note: to stem a flow is to check or stop it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An inspection is said to include where the energy comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam drove engines and turbines, so it is a classic source of motive power.

clue.text: Chap packing weapon in trousers, say

indicators.note: packing means holding something inside, as a case holds its contents

blocks.note: a gent is a man or chap
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A man is carrying a concealed gun in his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packing' is slang for carrying a gun, which hides its role as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are one example of a garment, an item of clothing; 'say' marks the example.
